articles.title_zh: Arrest made after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
facts_zh:
Arrest made after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
- Published
Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest.
Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 local time (19:15 GMT) on Friday and firefighters found it engulfed in flames.
No injuries were reported, while difficult terrain hindered efforts to extinguish the blaze.

articles.title_original: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
articles.title_zh: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
facts_zh:
Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
- Published
Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite internet network.

Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it.
This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said.

all_titles.en: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits

articles.title_original: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
articles.title_zh: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
facts_zh:
Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
- Published
Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease.
A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said.
Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added.

all_titles.en: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya

articles.title_original: British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas
articles.title_zh: British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas
facts_zh:
Mum dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea
- Published
A woman has died after attempting to rescue her two sons when they were swept away while snorkelling in the Bahamas.
The Royal Bahamas Police Force said officers on the island of Bimini launched an investigation into the sudden death of a 36-year-old British woman on Tuesday.

The force said it believed the woman - thought to be from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire - had been snorkelling with her husband and two sons near the southern point of the island when a strong current reportedly swept both children away.

all_titles.en: British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas

articles.title_zh: Seven missing after multi-storey building collapses in Kenya's capital
facts_zh:
Seven missing after multi-storey building collapses in Kenya's capital
- Published
A search and rescue effort is under way to find seven people feared trapped under rubble after a building collapsed in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi.
Dramatic footage shows the bottom floor of the block, thought to have been 16 or 18 storeys, giving way before the rest of the building crumples, sending a plume of dust into the surrounding streets.
Dozens of builders had been working on the upper floors when it collapsed, but managed to emerge largely unscathed.

articles.title_zh: Minneapolis withdrawal was 'surrender', Trump's ex-border patrol chief tells BBC
facts_zh:
Minneapolis withdrawal was 'surrender', Trump's ex-border patrol chief tells BBC
- Published
The former US border patrol chief who became the public face of the highly controversial deportation drive in Minneapolis earlier this year has defended the operation, describing the withdrawal of agents from the city as a "surrender" by the Trump administration.
Greg Bovino also told the BBC that he was "not responding" to a lawsuit filed by the family of a woman shot dead during the operation.
He appeared to dismiss the legal action, praising the officers deployed to Minneapolis and saying "people do lawsuits all the time".

- Published
An oil spill from a tanker attacked near the Strait of Hormuz is spreading along the United Arab Emirates (UAE) coastline, forcing the closure of some beaches and coastal areas.

Satellite images from Monday show the beginnings of the oil spill from a ship matching the location and dimensions of Gem No.2, which was damaged between 9 and 10 October during a record surge of vessel strikes by Iran.
The slick of oil had spread more than 35km (22 miles) from the tanker by Wednesday, the satellite imagery showed.

facts_zh: Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.

The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria.
The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.
